title: Explainable AI supported hybrid deep learning method for layer 2 intrusion detection
researchArea: Layer-2 Network Intrusion Detection / Explainable AI (XAI)
problem: Lack of specialized benchmark datasets and intrusion detection frameworks targeting Layer-2 network attacks (e.g., ARP Spoofing, DHCP Starvation, MAC Flooding, STP Root Bridge) occurring within local internal networks.
motivation: Existing IDS datasets predominantly focus on upper-layer OSI protocols (Layers 3–7), leaving internal corporate networks vulnerable to undetectable Layer-2 disruptions and unauthorized access.
noveltyAndContributions: Constructed and released the CL2-IDS benchmark dataset containing 49 features across 10 classes (9 Layer-2 attack vectors + normal traffic).
Proposed a novel hybrid CNN + Bi-LSTM deep learning architecture operating on 3x3x1 grayscale image representations of local network feature vectors.
Applied SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) to explain feature contributions and decision-making mechanisms across distinct attack classes.
methodology: Captured network traffic PCAP files across simulated corporate local network attack scenarios using Wireshark and Tshark.
Extracted a common set of 9 key network features across all attack classes to prevent model overfitting and reduce computational load.
Normalized tabular features using QuantileTransformer (scaled to 0–255) and reshaped them into 3x3x1 grayscale image samples.
Passed images through 3 Conv2D layers (64, 128, 256 filters of size 1x1 with ReLU and MaxPooling2D), flattened spatial maps, and fed them into a Bi-LSTM layer (64 cells).
Classified outputs using a 128-neuron Dense layer with Softmax activation over 10 target classes, trained with the Adam optimizer and categorical cross-entropy loss.
keyAssumptions: Tabular Layer-2 network traffic features can be effectively modeled as 3x3 grayscale images to leverage combined CNN spatial and Bi-LSTM sequential feature extraction.
A selected subset of 9 common network features provides sufficient discriminative power across diverse Layer-2 attack vectors.
datasets: CL2-IDS Dataset (constructed by author, ~100,000 samples, 10 classes)
experimentalSetup: 80/20 train/test data split over 50 training epochs
Python 3.12.4 with Keras, TensorFlow, OpenCV, and Matplotlib
Hardware platform: 32 GB RAM, 1 TB SSD
xaiEvaluation: Visualized feature contribution maps (positive/red vs. negative/blue impact) across classes, identifying frame.cap_len and frame.len as critical features for differentiating attack vectors.
results: The hybrid CNN + Bi-LSTM model achieved an overall classification accuracy of 95.28% (Precision: 0.95, Recall: 0.95, F1-Score: 0.95). 100% precision was achieved for DoS Smurf, DHCP Starvation, DoS SYN Flood, ARP Spoof, STP Root Bridge, and Rogue DHCP classes.
failureConditions: High attribute similarity in frame length features (frame.cap_len and frame.len) caused misclassifications and transitions among Telnet Brute Force, RDP Brute Force, MAC Flood, and Normal traffic classes.
costEvaluation: Used compact 3x3 image inputs with 1x1 convolutional filters to minimize feature space size, model parameters, and computational complexity.

limitations.text: Overlap in packet length attributes led to reduced classification precision for Telnet Brute Force (84%), RDP Brute Force (88%), and MAC Flood (83%) classes.
Dataset generation was conducted on a simplified, single-switch local network topology rather than a multi-segment distributed enterprise deployment.
The paper focuses solely on centralized deep learning and does not incorporate federated learning or distributed client architectures.

futureWork: Expand network design and topologies to build a broader, multi-segment dataset.
Incorporate data collected directly from switch hardware using specialized algorithms.
Develop Layer-2 detection end-user applications and extend SHAP explanations to application-layer attacks.
relevance: Directly relevant to the Layer-2 Intrusion Detection and Explainable AI (XAI) pillars of your thesis subject, providing a dedicated dataset (CL2-IDS) and SHAP evaluation framework.
newIdeas: Adapt the CL2-IDS dataset and CNN + Bi-LSTM + SHAP framework into a Federated Learning architecture across heterogeneous network segments.

evidence.item: SHAP feature explainability & class transitivity analysis
